reason: The cited evidence does not address tungsten, fusion conditions, or the proposed synergy. E1 shows a strength-ductility trade-off in an ultrafine-grained alloy, not improved toughness, and E2 describes dynamic recovery in a different material, with no mention of grain-boundary sliding or dislocation climb synergy.
premises: Nanostructuring tungsten increases grain boundary density.
High grain boundary density enables grain-boundary sliding at high temperatures.
Grain-boundary sliding synergistically enhances dislocation climb.
Combined sliding and climb produce uniform plastic deformation and improved toughness.
Coarse-grained tungsten lacks these mechanisms and exhibits lower ductility/toughness.
